newsitem.title: USA: Alitalia sees JFK trade fall, now mulls surcharge.
newsitem.headline: Alitalia sees JFK trade fall, now mulls surcharge.

text.p: Alitalia Airlines is waiting to see if jet fuel prices drop to the levels of June last year before removing the carg fuel surcharge, said its North American marketing manager Ross Pizzillo.
But if many of the other carriers remove their charges, Alitalia would follow suit, he added.
Pizzillo estimates that 50,000 tonnes of cargo is exported from the U.S. to Italy on a yearly basis.

"Alitalia is probably responsible for 55 percent of that market share." Approximately 120,000 tonnes is imported to the U.S. from various gates in Italy, and Alitalia is probably responsible for about 30 percent of that, he said.

Alitalia's exports from Kennedy dropped 15 percent in Jan-Feb 1997 against the same period 1996. Its imports fell 29 percent at JFK. Pizzillo said that the removal of a 747 freighter flights out of JLK at the start of 1997 was the main reason for the fall.
Beginning March 30 the carrier, as part of its summer schedule, will fly two additional routes. New York to Milan using a Boeing 767, and New York to Rome on a Boeing 747.
It will also maintain a 747 freighter flight from Kennedy to Chicago's O'Hare before returning to various gates in Italy five days a week. The summer schedule will be in effect to October 26.
The carrier, in a co-share with Continental Airlines, saw a four percent increase in exports and 30 percent increase in imports at Newark International airport in Jan-Feb.

The additional flights from Newark as part its summer schedule include two flights to Rome and one to Milan, all three using McDonnell Douglas DC-10 aircraft. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
